newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT-Dlr eyes more consolidation, may go lower.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Dlr eyes more consolidation, may go lower.

text.p: Dollar/yen will likely remain consolidative near term, but chartists warned of a bias to slide even lower.
Joseph Klettner, a foreign exchange technical analyst at Chase Securities Inc, pegged good resistance at 114.10 yen, but cautioned a true break of that level would require even further gains.
"If we can't break through (114.10) by getting above 114.50, then I think, we'll see further consolidation from the week's high of 114.92," Klettner said.
Klettner noted that consolidation can initially take the dollar lower to 112.75 yen, a level of chart congestion.
The dollar managed to briefly hit 114.18 yen on Thursday but 114.50 remained elusive.
In afternoon dealings, the dollar traded near 114.02/07 yen, up from 113.65/68 at the open.
Michael Zentz of Pegasus Econometric Group emphasized the dollar's outlook remains bullish longer term, but he also warned of potential for a deeper correction lower.

A break below support at 112.60 yen, a 38.2 percent Fibonacci retracement of the move from 108.90 in September to 114.88 in October, could leave the dollar targeting 112.00 at a minimum and 111.00 as well, said Zentz, a director of technical research at Pegasus.
Zentz said he is a "little more constructive" currently on dollar/mark.
He sketched support at 1.5010 marks and 1.5050 marks, which he deemed a 50 percent Fibonacci retracement of the rally from 1.4650 in July to 1.5445 in October.
Zentz predicted both support levels should hold and provide dollar/mark a "nice little bounce from here if not much more".
The U.S. currency traded around 1.5184/89 marks in late dealings, up from 1.5144/47 marks at the open.
Klettner noted that a convincing break of resistance at 1.5150 would require the dollar to push above 1.5187.
Should that happen, he said the dollar could retest the October high of 1.5454 in the next few weeks.
